questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Their range of public health related courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In regards to information provided by host university, it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy, it is very difficult to find housing in Sydney for a short period if you don't wish to pay a lot of money. Recommendations: find housing after arriving in Sydney, have a hostel/hotel booked for a couple of weeks upon arrival and then look for rooms on flatmates or anything similar.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You won't have a connection to what happens on campus, e.g. events and activities, especially if you live further away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was told by UNSW that on-campus housing was not an option for exchange students, yet when I arrived I met several exchange students from Scandinavia who were all staying on campus, and they had no problems applying for on-campus housing. Maybe be a bit more clear about what is actually possible as an exchange student.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The application process was relatively easy, and I just had to follow a list of things they needed, such as different documents from UCPH, Visa, medical insurance etc. There were not any problems there. I don't remember any other form of registration process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university staff

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure. Just follow the university's instructions. Host university was really good at provided detailed instructions on how and when to apply for classes etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: With everything being in an Australian context made it a bit more difficult, but in a different way. The level was still significantly lower than at UCPH. For MA courses at least.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on the professor. Some of them did not leave time for class discussions, which we have at UCPH, whereas some courses were pretty much only class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Technologies
Health Orgs, Strategy & Change
Comparative Health Care Systems
Politics, Surveillance, Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Politics, Surveillance, Health is a course that challenges your way of thinking of politics and how health is perceived and handled in politics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was a lot more expensive that I expected. However, local transportation was a lot cheaper that I had thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs, and they also had Funner Summer for international and exchange students, which are small and very inexpensive trips around places in and outside of Sydney, e.g. a trip to the Blue Mountains or the South Coast.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Funner Summer. Very fun, very inexpensive, and you meet a lot of other students from different countries and faculties.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can around New South Wales, other states and territories, and other countries nearby. Flights are cheaper in Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, it is not very different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really. Usually international and exchange students stick together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Understanding the accent.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are a lot more kind to strangers than Danes are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't expect the educational level to be extremely high, so you shouldn't necessarily choose courses you view as "safe" options. 
Don't expect a final exam by the end of the course, you will have assignments throughout the course, which will count for your final grade.
Attend the dinner for international and exchange students, it is a great way to meet other students who are also new to everything there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about public health from the perspectives of my classmates, who were mostly international students from third world countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be so far away from everything I was used to, and still manage.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
